Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells

MYP 4 Science · MYP 4 / Grade 9 Biology · Criterion A · 39 marks · 75 minutes · Prepared by Mr George Apidi
Guiding question: A human, a maize plant, a bacterium and a dog look nothing alike. What do they all have in common, and where are the differences hiding?
🎯 Start here

Your mitochondria carry their own DNA, which is a clue to their history. What might they have been before they lived inside your cells?

STEP 1 · QUESTION

What do they have in common? What is a cell?

0 – 20 min · Starter and Engage
Think, pair, share
Your teacher shows you four living things: a human, a maize plant, a bacterium and a dog. They look completely different. THINK on your own for one minute · PAIR with your partner for two · SHARE with the class for two.

In your book, then here

1(a). What do you think is the smallest unit that makes up your body? [1]
Support hintYour honest idea is fine.
1(b). Write TWO things that all four living things have in common. [2]
Support hintOne mark each. The big one: what are they all made of?

What is a cell?

  • A CELL is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
  • "Structural" means cells are what living things are built from.
  • "Functional" means cells do the jobs that keep an organism alive: they are not just building blocks.
  • CELL THEORY: 1. All living organisms are made of one or more cells. 2. The cell is the basic unit of life. 3. All cells come from cells that already exist.

In your book, then here

2. A brick wall is made of bricks. Explain, in one sentence, why a cell is MORE than just a brick. [2]
Support hintA brick only holds the wall up… …but what does a cell DO?
This step: 5 marks
STEP 2 · EXPLORE

Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells

20 – 32 min · Criterion A

🎬 Videos for this lesson

▶ Prokaryotic vs eukaryotic cellsListen for where the DNA is kept: that is the difference everything else follows from.
  • ALL cells have a cell membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA. The big difference is WHERE THE DNA IS KEPT.
  • Bacteria DO have DNA. It is simply not inside a nucleus: it floats in the cytoplasm as a single loop.
  • A PROKARYOTE has no membrane-bound organelles at all. A EUKARYOTE has a nucleus and many others, each doing its own job.

STEP 4 · EXPLAIN

Discussion: why are cells so different?

Your group question

In your book, then here

5. Write your group's best answer in two or three sentences. [3]
Support hintWhat do all cells share? What is different about what they do? How does a cell's structure relate to its job?
How we found out: a short history
In 1665 Robert Hooke looked at thin cork through an early microscope and saw tiny empty boxes. He called them "cells", after the small rooms in a monastery. A few years later Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, who ground his own lenses, became the first person to see living microorganisms. Cell theory came much later: Schleiden and Schwann in 1838–39, completed by Virchow and Remak in the 1850s with the idea that cells come from other cells. Remak published it first, but was rarely credited at the time. The point: nobody could see a cell until the technology existed to magnify one. Better glass and lenses, work many cultures contributed to over centuries, changed what scientists could know.
This step: 3 marks
STEP 5 · CHALLENGE

Cell classification challenge

55 – 66 min · Criterion A
Work with a partner
For each cell, decide what type it is and give your evidence: "It has ______, so it must be ______." One is easier than it looks: read all the clues before you decide.
CellDescription
AAbout 2 µm across. Has a cell wall, a cell membrane and ribosomes. Its DNA is a single loop floating in the cytoplasm. There is no nucleus.
BAbout 40 µm across. Has a nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes and a cell membrane. No cell wall. Its shape is irregular.
CAbout 60 µm across and box-shaped. Has a nucleus, mitochondria, a cell wall, chloroplasts and one large vacuole in the middle.
DAbout 30 µm across. Has a nucleus, mitochondria and a cell wall, but no chloroplasts and no large central vacuole. It absorbs food from dead material around it.
